title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: K is a number field and Gamma = Gal(Kbar/K). U_{0,3} = P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}. I_0 is a finite set of K-rational base points, possibly tangential, in U_{0,3}(K). The object studied is the profinite fundamental groupoid Pi^_1(U_{0,3}; I_0). Each u in Gamma acts on it, fixing the objects, since the points of I_0 are K-rational.

The page closes the previous parenthesis. The difficulty there was that the fibre over I_0 in a cover need not consist of K-rational points. The remedy proposed is to replace Gamma by a suitable open subgroup Gamma'.

It then turns the descent picture into a test. It seeks necessary conditions for an automorphism Theta of the groupoid Pi^_1(U_{0,3}; I_0), fixing the vertices, to come from some u in Gamma. The condition is as follows.
- Take any finite étale cover f: C -> U_{0,3} defined over K.
- Put I = f^{-1}(I_0) ∩ C(K), the K-rational points over the base points.
- Then Theta must lift to an automorphism Theta_C of Pi^_1(C, I). The lift must be the identity on the vertices I and compatible with Pi^_1(C,I) -> Pi^_1(U_{0,3},I_0).

By the injectivity of Hom_{Pi_1(C)}(x,y) -> Hom_{Pi_1(U)}(f x, f y) noted on the previous page, such a lift is unique if it exists.

The condition is said to take a sharper form when I -> I_0 is surjective. Since the full fibre is generally not rational, there is a weakened condition, which is the open-subgroup version. For each étale cover there must be a power Theta^n (n ≥ 1) satisfying the previous conditions with I = f^{-1}(I_0), the whole fibre. This is legitimate for Theta = u: u has some power in the normal core of the open stabiliser of the fibre points, because Gamma modulo that core is finite.

The margin asks how these conditions depend on I_0. The next page adds a further condition: the action must preserve kernels of maps pi_1(C) -> pi_1(X) for intermediate quotient curves. It then states a lemma on lifting automorphisms along injective-on-pi_1 groupoid maps.

Overall, this is a programme for characterising the image of Gamma in Aut(Pi^_1(U_{0,3}; rational base points)). The characterisation is by liftability to the whole tower of K-defined covers, with their K-rational points kept as base points. It is a precursor of GT-type and Ihara/Oda–Matsumoto-type 'tower' characterisations of Galois.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The weakened 'power Theta^n' condition is correct for Theta coming from Gamma, since every element of a profinite group has a power in any given open normal subgroup. The exponent n depends on the cover C, which the text does not state explicitly.
The statement of what happens when I -> I_0 is (non-)surjective is garbled or incomplete on the page. It is unclear whether an extra condition is meant or the condition simply becomes stronger.

ideas.what: Necessary condition for an automorphism of the profinite fundamental groupoid of P^1-{0,1,infinity} with rational base points to be Galois: it must lift, fixing vertices, to the groupoid of every K-defined étale cover, based at its K-rational points over I_0.
ideas.modern_name: Characterisation of the Galois image in Aut/Out of pi_1 via the tower of covers (Ihara/Oda–Matsumoto-type, 'GT-like' conditions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT, 1990); Ihara (1990s); Oda–Matsumoto conjecture (I/OM); Pop (proof of I/OM); Harbater–Schneps on automorphisms of the tower
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller tower and the hope of describing the Galois image combinatorially. This specific covering-tower/rational-base-point formulation is not there to my knowledge.

ideas.what: Weakened condition: some power Theta^n satisfies the lifting condition for the full fibre f^{-1}(I_0), mirroring the passage to an open subgroup Gamma'.
ideas.modern_name: Passage to open subgroups in Galois-action criteria; 'virtual' Galois-equivariance

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the vertex-fixing lift, via injectivity of Hom-sets in the groupoid map for a covering.

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, well before Drinfeld/Ihara/Oda–Matsumoto, a test for Galois-ness of an automorphism of pi^_1(P^1-{0,1,inf}). The test is that the automorphism lifts compatibly through all K-defined covers, using the groupoid based at the K-rational points of those covers. Rational points act as rigidifying 'Gamma-fixed vertices' throughout the tower. This merges the tower-characterisation of Galois (later I/OM, Pop) with the rational-point/section viewpoint (anabelian section conjecture) in a single groupoid framework. Published GT-type definitions mostly use only tangential base points at the cusps of moduli spaces.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This yields a candidate 'arithmetic GT' subgroup cut out by rational-point-based groupoid conditions over the Belyi tower. Whether it equals the image of G_K is a natural open-style question related to the work of Pop and of Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki. It is not standard in the literature in this form.

missed.claim: The dependence of the conditions on the choice of the base-point set I_0 is flagged in the margin but not pursued.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This concerns whether adding rational base points (or tangential points) strictly shrinks the candidate group. It is analogous to comparing GT-type groups defined with different base-point data.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early, explicit groupoid formulation of a 'liftability to all K-defined covers with rational base points' criterion for the Galois image. It anticipates themes of Ihara/Oda–Matsumoto and Pop, and the rational-point flavour is somewhat distinctive. However, it is only a set of necessary conditions sketched in programme form, and the general idea is consonant with the Esquisse.
